reason: I'll fit the salivary glands to start building the digestive system and connect them to the mouth.
expectation: The glands will attach to the digestive tube, leaving the other slots available.

alternatives.reason: Starting starch digestion also fits the goal, but I want to assemble the organs first.

effect: The glands are fitted, and the result clarifies what each digestive organ supplies. I’ll continue assembling the tube.
reaction: The short explanation connects the organ fittings to digestion, though the fitting itself was predictable.
reason: The pancreas is another named fitting and supplies digestive juices.
expectation: The pancreas will fit into the digestive tube, leaving the liver and portal vessel slots available.

alternatives.reason: The liver and gallbladder also belong on the tube, but I chose the pancreas first.

effect: The pancreas is fitted, so I’ll finish adding the available digestive organs.
reason: The liver and gallbladder are the remaining available organ fitting.
expectation: They will attach to the digestive tube, leaving the portal vessel slot for later.

effect: The digestive organs are fitted and their goal is complete, so I’ll turn to breaking down the meal.
reason: Salivary amylase starts starch digestion, connecting the fitted glands to their function.
expectation: The starch will be partly broken down, perhaps requiring further enzymes before absorption.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the remaining goal, but I chose to start with starch.

effect: Salivary amylase produced shorter starch chains, so further digestion is still needed.
reaction: The intermediate product makes the sequence clear.
reason: I’ll continue starch digestion with the remaining enzymes.
expectation: The shorter chains will be broken into smaller sugars suitable for absorption.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the meal goal, but I want to finish the starch sequence first.

effect: Starch digestion has produced individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining; I’ll move on to another food component.
reaction: The two-stage sequence clearly connects starch breakdown to absorption.
reason: Protein-digesting enzymes should break protein into smaller components for absorption.
expectation: The protein will be broken into smaller pieces, possibly amino acids.

alternatives.reason: Fat digestion also advances the goal, but I chose protein first.

effect: Protein digestion produced amino acids, leaving fat digestion as the only offered combination.
reaction: The result was predictable and clearly shows the protein chains broken down.
reason: I’ll digest the remaining fat to advance the meal goal.
expectation: Bile and lipase will help break the fat into smaller components suitable for absorption.

effect: Fat digestion produced fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the meal breakdown goal. The explanation clarified that bile disperses fat while lipase breaks it apart.
reaction: The distinction between bile and lipase was useful and more informative than the fitting steps.

mostWorthwhile.text: The two-stage starch sequence was most worthwhile: it showed starch becoming shorter chains and then individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the pancreas and then the liver and gallbladder felt predictable and repetitive, with little new information in the individual results.

surprise.text: The fat digestion result clarified that bile disperses fat into droplets but is not an enzyme; lipase breaks the fat molecules apart.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the order of fitting the pancreas and liver was a choice between equally plausible steps.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in continuing to see how the digested nutrients are absorbed and connected to the body, although I would hope for fewer repetitive fittings.
